title: 8-round AES-192: Impossible differential, high-data endpoint

target.description: Standard AES-192 under the paper's round numbering: initial whitening k0, rounds1 onward; last MixColumns omitted for 8-round recovery variants. Guess7 bytes0,7,10,13,4,8,12 of k8 and byte3 of w7, then recover8 whitening bytes:128 bits of named subkey material. These are selected round-key values, not an independently priced complete192-bit master key.

setting.key_relation: Two unknown AES-192 master keys K and K'=K XOR Delta, where Delta[0]=Delta[8]=a!=0 and the other22 bytes are0. Initial whitening is k0; round subkeys are k1,... .
setting.key_population: General unknown key pair with attacker-chosen nonzero a; b,c are actual key-dependent S-box output differences, not independently chosen subkeys.
setting.plaintext_model: 2^47 structures, each using2^65 queries across two keys. A2^-104 filter yields2^71 retained pairs per terminal guess.
assumptions: The source models pair filters and incorrect whitening-key eliminations probabilistically; those independence assumptions have not been proved for every AES key.
Named subkey bits may be dependent. No complete192-bit master-key recovery budget is supplied.
The source uses64 memory accesses per encryption equivalent; this is an accounting convention, not an independent implementation measurement.
The64-bit terminal guess determines b but not c;127 feasible c hypotheses are approximated by factor2^7 in time, without extra keys or data.

time.note: Source formula uses2^71 retained pairs,2^64 terminal hypotheses, a2^-6 memory-access conversion and factor2^7 c enumeration. Remaining master-key completion is not priced.

data.note: Total plaintext-block encryption queries across exactly2 related keys, not a per-key budget.

memory.note: Section5.2 reuses the Section4 table, whose stated requirement is2^69 bytes; peak memory for this eight-round variant is not separately reported.

preprocessing.note: The shared Section4 precomputation is about2^62 encryptions; no complete additional setup total for this extension is separately supplied.

success.description: The128-bit output consists of64 terminal/equivalent subkey bits and64 whitening bits. Section5.2 Third Attack assigns2^47 two-pool structures, mean mprime=2^71 pairs per guess and127 feasible c hypotheses. The source inherited wrong-whitening model over all2^64 outer guesses and all c trials gives E_model W <= 127*2^128 exp(-128). Its2^112-query/2^136-time assignment already charges c enumeration. This is not transferred from the first/second eight-round variants with their separate unresolved difference-filter conflict. Derived first-moment lower bound within the source random-filter model for a unique correct complete stated partial-subkey output. It is not an author-printed aggregate percentage, an experimental rate, or a proved actual-AES success probability; no full master-key recovery is asserted. Correct-tuple retention plus P_model(W>=1)<=E_model W supplies the implication without independence between different wrong tuples or auxiliary trials. The repeated-filter uniformity/independence assumptions are inherited from the source; the source also substitutes mean retained-pair counts for random counts, which is not justified as an actual-cipher upper bound by this audit.

review.scope: Verified exact-edition source extraction, full stored-output and same-budget loop mapping, right-candidate retention and first-moment arithmetic. Independent source-first and endpoint review. This verifies the conditional model inference, not actual-cipher random-filter assumptions, mean-count substitution, attack reproduction or a new full-paper audit.

evidence.interpretation: No numerical recovery success is supplied for this 128-bit named-subkey output. The source uses2^71 useful pairs and a small conditional wrong-list estimate; it does not quantify joint output recovery. The64-bit terminal guess determines b;127 feasible c hypotheses are additional time, not a new key-pair probability. Remaining master-key completion stays unpriced.

evidence.interpretation: Aggregate lower bound derived within the source model, retaining the existing exact output, conditions, resource assignment and all scientific conflicts. The inequality applies to the model, not to the real cipher without proving the source assumptions.

limitations: Independent local checks cover the AES key schedule and deterministic components. Full cryptanalytic searches, resource calibration and success rates have not been reproduced.
